result:
All 17 tests pass. The build reports JUnit 3.8.2, consistent with the `junit.framework.TestCase` style used throughout the project.

Summary of what I did:
- Read `ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.java` and cross-checked its collaborators (`Excluder`, `ConstructorConstructor`, `Primitives`, `TypeAdapters.INTEGER`) to understand the exact semantics of `excludeField`, the anti-recursion `writeField` check, the primitive-null-skip logic in `read`, and the duplicate-field-name error path.
- Matched existing conventions from `JsonTreeWriterTest.java`, `JsonElementReaderTest.java`, and `ObjectTypeAdapterTest.java`: JUnit 3 (`extends TestCase`), `try { ...; fail(); } catch (X expected) {}` for exceptions, and driving adapters via `toJson`/`fromJson`.
- Wrote `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/internal/bind/ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactoryAgentTest.java` with 17 tests covering: adapter creation for POJOs/primitives/interfaces, round-trip serialization, null read/write, unknown-field skipping, `@SerializedName` (including alternates), duplicate-name `IllegalArgumentException`, transient/static field exclusion, self-reference recursion avoidance, primitive-vs-boxed null handling, field inheritance ordering, and the public `excludeField` method directly.
- Verified with `defects4j compile` and ran the suite directly — all 17 tests pass.
